claims.quote: Inspector Rao and I prised up the study's low hearth strip; it came away complaining. Behind it was a narrow pocket, black with old soot and the kind of neatness houses give to things they'd rather forget.
Nestled there was a compact clockwork — tiny plates of brass, a wound spring and a cam-driven push-rod — its surfaces darkened where oil had pooled.
The oil on its plates matched the smudge on the watch-case Clara—no, Evelyn—had been holding.
One brass plate bore a tiny filing nick, a maker's tic I had seen on pieces worked at Derek Lyle's bench.
An aluminium extension ladder leaned against the boundary wall; one rung carried a fresh scrape consistent with being used to reach the coal-hatch.
The external coal chute hatch's bolt showed recent abrasion and coal dust in the latch groove.
"In the morning room — same chair by the hearth; I was reading the paper. Ask Marta; she brought my tea." He glanced to Marta; his throat tightened.
"I was serving breakfast. I put his tea down in the kitchen at nine; he wasn't in the morning room." She pressed her lips and, under her breath, muttered, "She said he'd taken money."
"In the shed. Been filing brass all morning — had a stubborn plate this morning." He looked at the disassembled clockwork and his hand went to his shirt as if for a tool.

When Rao moved away to brief his sergeant, I closed my notebook and set a small list against the case: secure and photograph the clockwork, photograph the hatch and ladder, get access to Derek's bench and request a copy of Evelyn's ledger.
"She said he'd taken money." (Marta's muttered aside when asked about Henry being in the morning room.)

promises.promise: Obtain a copy of Evelyn's ledger for inspection and to check for debts or payments.
